articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document is the "SJAA EPHEMERIS," the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association, dated November 1992. It is identified as Volume 3, Number 11, indicating a regular, likely monthly, release from the organization.

articles.title: The Eye Piece
articles.summary: Bob Madden details his correspondence with Lech Jaszowski, a 20-year-old Polish astronomy student, and seeks donations of astronomy periodicals and hardware (like eyepieces and mirrors) to send him, while being cautious about shipping costs and customs. The article also provides a calendar of upcoming club events, including numerous star parties, general meetings with featured speakers, and board of directors meetings scheduled from November through January.

articles.title: Three nights at Fremont Peak
articles.summary: This article details the first two nights of a three-night stargazing event at Fremont Peak, highlighting the excellent observing conditions despite some smog. It describes the various telescopes present, a good turnout of attendees including families, and specific observing attempts like viewing the Orion Nebula and the elusive Horsehead Nebula. The report emphasizes the stable and pleasant weather, along with the camaraderie among observers.

articles.title: The Polish Amateur Astronomers Society (PTMA)
articles.summary: The Polish Amateur Astronomers Society (PTMA), founded in 1927, serves as the central organization for amateur astronomers in Poland. Headquartered in Cracow, it has grown to 3,000 members across 25 regional departments, offering lectures, public shows, workshops, and publishing the monthly magazine *Urania*. The society includes six specialized sections, with the Section of Observations of Positions and Occultations being particularly active, conducting numerous observations and publishing its own materials.

articles.title: Astronomical Clubs
articles.summary: The article highlights the scarcity of astronomical clubs in Poland compared to the United States, identifying only two known examples. One is Helvius, active since 1987 in Tranow, catering to young people aged 10-19 with weekly theoretical and manual training, alongside school programs. The second is a correspondence club located in Silesia.

articles.title: Magazines
articles.summary: The article describes *Urania*, a 32-page monthly astronomy magazine published by the PTMA, which began in March 1922 and has issued 608 numbers. It aims to provide information to amateur astronomers, uncover astronomical mysteries, and inspire active participation in the amateur scientific movement through diverse articles, observer guides, and historical insights. Unfortunately, the PTMA's poor financial situation jeopardizes the magazine's continued publication.

articles.title: Double, Triple and Multiple Stars
articles.summary: Patrick M. Donnelly recounts his experiences observing double and multiple stars using only 7x50 binoculars and a star field guide while on field work in Iowa. He details numerous binocular-resolvable stellar systems, including Nu-Draconis, Epsilon and Delta Lyra, Mu and Omicron-1 Cygni, and various pairs in Capricorn and Andromeda. The article highlights that many interesting celestial objects can be observed effectively with limited equipment, providing a practical guide for binocular astronomy.

articles.title: Paul Barton's Star Party Report
articles.summary: This report details a highly successful star party in 1992, possibly one of the best of the year, attended by many individuals including Rick Morales with his 20" Dobson telescope. Excellent viewing conditions continued through Sunday night, enjoyed by a smaller, dedicated group of observers.

articles.title: Houge Park Star Party
articles.summary: A star party was held at Houge Park on Friday, October 2nd, attended by six to eight telescopes and approximately 50 guests, despite initial hazy conditions. Attendees viewed various celestial objects including the Moon, Saturn, several nebulae, and galaxies, with Jerry McKee ably operating the JMI-18 telescope. The event also highlighted upcoming plans for a student visit and acknowledged Mark Wagner's contribution to the Ephemeris publication.

articles.title: September Slide and Equipment Night
articles.summary: The 'September Slide and Equipment Night' event at Houge Park featured members showcasing their custom-built astronomical equipment. Highlights included Bob Elsberry's 5.5" Lensless Wright for visual observation, Jeff Horne's 8" Lensless Wright Camera, Jack Zeiders presenting a new Hydrogen Alpha filter and solar telescope, and Ernie Piini's self-designed solar eclipse telescope. All photographs were taken by Bob Keller, capturing the innovative spirit of the participants.

articles.title: Houge Park Star Party
articles.summary: The article reports on the Houge Park Star Party, an astronomical observing event that took place in November 1992. It highlights an attendee, Paul Barton, and his JMI-18 telescope.

articles.title: Houge Park Star Parties
articles.summary: This document features 'Houge Park Star Parties,' including several images of individuals with telescopes and engaging in astronomy discussions at these events. It also presents the complete 1993 calendar for the SJAA, detailing dates for General Meetings, Houge Park Star Parties, and Beginning Astronomy Classes, as published in the November 1992 'Ephemeris.'

articles.title: EQUIPMENT LOAN STATUS
articles.summary: This document outlines the current status of an equipment loan program for members, primarily focusing on telescopes. Members are invited to bid for available telescopes or request renewal of current loans, with a table detailing each piece of equipment, its borrower, and the loan date. The list includes various telescope types like reflectors, Dobsons, Maksutovs, and SCTs.

articles.title: Paul Barton's Star Party Report
articles.summary: Paul Barton's Star Party Report details a successful event at St. Clare's School, attended by approximately 50 parents, students, and teachers. Attendees viewed the sun during the day and several celestial objects like Saturn, Andromeda, and Hercules at night, despite bright moonlight. The event also featured a talk by Jack Peterson, ample food, and involvement from SJAA members, with a call for more volunteers to support future star parties.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: ASTRO ADS is a free classifieds section for noncommercial advertisers to sell astronomically related products or services. Ads must be submitted by the 12th of each month to Bob Madden and will run for approximately three months. The article includes several example listings for used telescopes, eyepieces, mounts, and other astronomy accessories.

articles.title: Lunar Phases Date Rise Tran Set
articles.summary: This document outlines the schedule for the major lunar phases during November, providing the exact time and date for each event. For every phase, including First Quarter, Full Moon, Last Quarter, and New Moon, it lists the corresponding moonrise, transit, and moonset times. This data is essential for observers to track the moon's visibility and position throughout the month.

articles.title: Nearer Planets
articles.summary: This document provides an astronomical guide for several 'nearer planets'—Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn—along with data for the Sun (SOL). For three specific dates in November (7th, 17th, 27th), it lists each celestial body's distance in Astronomical Units (AU), apparent magnitude, and three corresponding time entries, likely indicating observation windows or key positions.

articles.title: Astronomical Twilight
articles.summary: This document presents a concise table of Julian Dates and corresponding Gregorian dates in November, each paired with a specific time range. These time ranges likely denote the start and end times of astronomical twilight for the listed dates.

articles.title: Sidereal Time
articles.summary: This document provides a concise listing of sidereal times corresponding to specific dates in November, referenced to Pacific Standard Time (PST). It details the sidereal time at transit right ascension for November 7th and 17th, and the sidereal time at local midnight for November 27th. This data likely serves as a quick reference for astronomical observation planning.

articles.title: Darkest Saturday Night Nov 21
articles.summary: The article announces the "Darkest Saturday Night" on November 21st, providing key astronomical times for optimal viewing. It details a sunset at 16:46 PST, twilight ending at 18:22 PST, and moonrise not until 04:38 PST, indicating excellent dark-sky observing conditions.

articles.title: Offices and Board of Directors | Ephemeris Contributors
articles.summary: This document lists the current Offices and Board of Directors, including their titles, names, and contact phone numbers. It also provides a separate list of 'Ephemeris Contributors' with their names and phone numbers, and identifies the Editor.

articles.title: Comet Comments
articles.summary: Don Machholtz's "Comet Comments" provides updates on several recently recovered or discovered comets, including Brewington, Helin-Lawrence, Tuttle, and Ciftreo, detailing their characteristics and expected visibility. The article highlights the significant recovery of Periodic Comet Swift-Tuttle, noting its rapid brightening, historical observations, upcoming perihelion, and its association with the Perseid meteor shower, providing an outlook for its next peak.

articles.title: EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document provides an ephemeris for Periodic Comet Swift-Tuttle (1992t) for the period from October 15 to December 9. It lists daily celestial coordinates (RA, DEC), elongation, sky position (Eastern sky), and estimated visual magnitude, serving as a guide for observers to track the comet's position and brightness changes.

articles.title: Can Anyone Help
articles.summary: A club is seeking assistance for a senior member who no longer drives and wishes to attend meetings at Milpitas Library. Members are requested to contact J.D. Wells, whose number is provided, to help arrange transportation.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP
articles.summary: This document outlines the membership options and associated fees for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), including regular, junior, and Sky & Telescope package memberships. It provides a fillable form for new members' personal details and instructions for submitting the application to the treasurer either at a meeting or by mail.

articles.title: MAKE CHECKS PAYABLE TO "SJAA"
articles.summary: This document outlines instructions for San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) membership payments, specifying various membership types and options for new or renewal. It also provides submission guidelines for the SJAA's monthly publication, "EPHEMERIS," including deadlines and editor contact information, along with the association's mailing address.

articles.title: SJAA HOTLINE
articles.summary: This document snippet advertises the "SJAA HOTLINE," a 24-hour information service provided by the SJAA organization. Dated November 1992 and referencing an "EPHEMERIS," it suggests the publication is likely from an astronomy club or society, offering timely astronomical information.
